questions.q: 1-(Aminomethyl)cyclohexan-1-ol is treated with NaNO₂ and dilute HCl in the cold. The main organic product is:
questions.explain: In this Tiffeneau–Demjanov reaction N₂ leaves, a ring bond shifts to the CH₂ carbon (ring grows to seven) and the oxygen-stabilised cation loses H⁺ to give the ketone.

questions.q: The reagent needed for a Demjanov rearrangement of a primary amine is:
options: NaNO₂ with HCl or acetic acid
questions.explain: The amine must be diazotised by nitrous acid made in situ from NaNO₂ and acid; nitric acid is a common wrong choice.

questions.q: Cyclobutylmethylamine reacts with nitrous acid in water. The ring-expanded product is:
questions.explain: With no OH next to the amine, the cation formed after the ring bond shifts is captured by water, giving cyclopentanol. Cyclobutylmethanol also forms, but it is the unrearranged product.

questions.q: Which sequence converts cyclohexanone into cycloheptanone?
questions.explain: The cyanohydrin is reduced to the 1,2-amino alcohol 1-(aminomethyl)cyclohexanol, which HNO₂ ring-expands to cycloheptanone. Hydrolysing the CN gives an acid with no NH₂ to diazotise.
